study.question: Observed limitation: target-relation content improves macro AUC from 0.8197867255 (g0-r0003-replica_control) to 0.8262472009 without explicit relation counts, and content+counts reaches 0.8275704846, while counts-only reaches 0.8200779142. The content/count factorial interaction is approximately +0.0010321 AUC, preliminary at one seed. The parent mixes feedback action embeddings inside DIN-weighted sums, but exposes only total relation counts explicitly. Does exposing the feedback composition specifically within a target relation improve prediction beyond its marginal count and feedback frequency? Earlier behavior-only grouping (g0-r0000-behavior_slots, 0.8136963424) trailed recency grouping (0.8183804941); retain recency rather than assuming behavior partitioning transfers. Field semantics also remained unsupported: atomic_fields 0.8195094317 trailed replica_seven 0.8197867255 despite beating coordinate_partition 0.8189680279. These were successful executions with negative comparative outcomes, not runtime failures.
study.hypothesis: Within each global/rank-quartile bin, four explicit unweighted historical feedback counts crossed with the seven existing target relations make positive feedback concentrated on matching entities directly accessible to token interaction. This may reduce cancellation and entanglement in the existing shared, signed DIN-weighted item/action sum. A gain over expected joint counts under conditional independence would support the usefulness of explicitly presenting this association, not new information or a proven novel mechanism.

nearest_work.difference: Closest local implementation is preserved. Add four explicit historical feedback channels per existing token; no new history events, token count, sequence grouping, attention layers or loss changes.

study.proposed_difference: For every existing [temporal bin, target relation] token, compute a four-vector c of counts of visible historical click/cart/fav/buy masks intersected with that bin and relation. Apply log1p(c)/log(101), then add a shared Linear(4,32,bias=False) to the unchanged slot projection before token identity and joint interaction. Modes joint/independent/marginal/zero differ only in count inputs. Positive encoded-ID equality retains parent padding/OOV caveats. No future action, new field, current label or external input is accessed. No originality is asserted; broader prior-art coverage of contingency statistics is unverified.
predictions: Main prediction: joint_feedback_counts exceeds both independent_feedback_counts and zero_feedback_counts on validation macro AUC; independent may improve over marginal if relation-conditioned magnitudes help. This is a directional prediction, not an undeclared per-task veto.

Provisional task prediction: cart and buy benefit more than click from explicit positive-feedback conjunctions; report fav and all four task AUC/Logloss deltas against parent and baseline even if they regress. Parent AUCs are click 0.6700841434, cart 0.8670683224, fav 0.8789302080, buy 0.8941992645; parent macro Logloss 0.0548851432.

Use only currently authorized existing history slices: empty, 1-16, 17-64, >64. Expect useful direct count signal in nonempty histories; larger empty-history gains cannot be directly attributed to this branch because count inputs are zero there. Training-induced changes can still affect empty histories. Report existing sample/positive/negative counts; empty buy has 13 positives and remains uncertain.

At fixed inherited parameters/input, all four modes have identical empty-history behavior; joint and independent agree for the global relation and for any relation covering every visible event of its bin. No-match relation joint/independent counts are zero while marginal can be positive.

All four new arms have predicted 32,944,901 parameters (31,793,216 embeddings, 1,151,685 dense), versus parent 32,944,773. Dense added parameters are 128 with no bias. Host must measure actual counts, peak memory, train/inference time and batch latency; no efficiency gain is claimed.
falsifiers: Joint failing to exceed independent leaves association-specific explicit-count value unsupported, even if joint exceeds zero. Marginal or independent winning favors a simpler explanation.
Zero matching or beating active modes rejects usefulness of this implementation under the fixed one-pass training recipe; it does not refute all feedback grouping or unified representations.

Any change to outputs when perturbing masked historical IDs/actions/task-mask entries or current target action, any nonfinite output/gradient, or failure of fixed-input parent-null equivalence invalidates the comparison until corrected.
A one-seed improvement that reverses in paired repetitions remains unstable. Deterministic replay of g0-r0003-replica_control and g0-r0002-replica_seven is not an independent seed replication.
alternative_explanations: Extra explicit statistics can improve optimization under one epoch without adding information; original weighted action embeddings already contain feedback/relation association.

Count-scale, sparsity, overlap and projection initialization can explain gains over conditional independence. A subsequent count-distribution-matched placebo would be necessary for stronger causal claims.

Auxiliary labels are user/category/brand matches within 24h, not ad-specific attributed conversions. Category/brand conjunction counts may exploit benchmark semantics and released offline feedback maturity; production time validity is not established.

Single-seed adaptation to one validation set and small slice positive counts can overstate differences. Host feedback has no user-cluster intervals or behavior/frequency/hour slices supplied here; do not invent them or claim significance.
Shared task towers can shift all slices during training even when the new branch is zero for a sample. Empty-history changes do not prove direct count effects.
